approach.method_basis: The Parent keeps every accepted score in a task-local archive for a fingerprint Gaussian process, but allows only the sixty-four highest-scoring accepted molecules to remain in its breeding population. It samples parents from three preferred score bands, generates a fresh pool through graph crossover and mutation, and selects evaluations using correlated posterior draws. Accepted offspring immediately compete for survival and can breed in later batches. This gives a functioning learning loop, while chemically distinct lower-scoring parents can disappear from the breeding population before their descendants are explored.
approach.novelty: Allocate survivor places in rounds across molecular cores: the best member of each core competes in the first round, the second-best members in the next, and so on until the existing population is full. Within a round, higher real scores win; the final survivors return to score order for the existing parent sampler. This protects several accepted core families while retaining the incumbent. The recorded lineage has tested posterior selection of generated offspring; this experiment changes the accepted molecules available for future breeding, with the inherited parent-draw rule intact.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-fc2c108a5253 reliably executes accepted-feedback posterior selection, but its complete three-replica evidence has only 565 strict best-parent beats among 4350 evaluated offspring, alongside concentrated useful chemical families. Its current macro mean is 0.5443738005952443 with population SD 0.013310111166991866. The all-accepted archive preserves labels, while greedy score-only survival can still remove distinct molecular cores from future breeding. A read-only reconstruction of all fifteen Parent task logs and accepted trajectory order finds 3540 capacity-limited survivor contests among 4350 accepted offspring; 1107 incoming accepted molecules are immediately rejected from the breeding population. On each identical contemporaneous Parent contest, score-ordered core-round survival changes the survivor set in 3083 cases, increases represented Murcko cores in 2260, retains 1008 of the 1107 rejected newcomers, and changes the immediate top-half breeding support in 209 cases. The incumbent is retained in every comparison. A simpler one-champion reservation with score-only fill changed lower memory but never immediate top-half support in these same records, motivating successive core rounds rather than assuming that any retained diversity reaches breeding. These comparisons expose an opportunity and supply no scores for alternative descendants or completed alternative trajectory. Cluster c-1e7b33da25 already establishes posterior execution while retaining weak descendant yield and concentrated chemistry as limitations.
hypothesis: Retain accepted breeding molecules by successive score-ordered rounds across Murcko cores, prioritizing each core's best member before any core's next member, then restore global score order for the unchanged parent sampler.

finding_summary.headline: Core-round survival broadened breeding, but protected records never bred and all three score replicas fell.
finding_summary.insights:
Preserving a low-ranked core and exploring it are separate events under the unchanged sampler. Of the 542 protected offspring, 116 survived into a later breeding state, but all remained below the sampled score bands. Six were still retained when the experiment ended and had first received protection in the terminal batch. The broader breeding came through changes to stronger analogues and the ranks of other survivors, rather than descendants of the directly protected records. A local support-promotion trace confirms that this indirect route can produce a parent-beating child, but such participation did not offset the overall loss in productive evaluations.

The actual trajectory also changes the apparent opportunity: on the already diversified Child states, only two incoming molecules were rescued from immediate greedy rejection, while 1,058 newcomers that local greedy selection would accept were excluded. Both rescued newcomers stayed outside breeding support. This narrows the result to a strong redistribution of survivor competition, with little evidence for the hoped-for exploration of protected weak parents. Mean generating-parent strength and mean offspring score both fell, so the smaller average parent deficit is not evidence of better candidates. The molecular assessment still finds repeated oversized heterocycle assemblies, tiny fragments, reactive bonds and constrained ring systems. Core coverage increased without resolving those chemical limitations. The passive greedy lists use existing labels only; they provide no alternate descendants or scores for an independently executed search.
finding_summary.results:
All 4,365 retention calls matched the declared core-round rule, preserved the incumbent and respected the 64-member capacity. Among 3,540 capacity-limited contests, 1,606 changed the local greedy survivor set and added one represented core; 1,266 also changed the immediate breeding support. Mean cores actually used per breeding batch rose from 12.98 to 24.20, and all fifteen final populations contained 64 distinct cores. There were 12,012 actual parent uses outside greedy breeding support reconstructed from the same accepted history. Those uses contributed to 326 evaluated offspring, including 35 best-parent beats and two incumbent gains.

The direct protection route remained unused: none of the 602 records retained against local greedy eviction, including 542 evaluated offspring, subsequently entered the breeding bands. Overall strict best-parent beats fell from 565/4,350 (12.99%) to 526/4,350 (12.09%), and incumbent gains fell from 218 to 175. Mean final-best score fell from 0.544374 to 0.514684, a paired change of -0.029690. All three seed deltas were negative, as were all five task means. The retention mechanism and changed breeding support are confirmed; the intended score improvement was not observed.

molecular.headline: Large repeated aromatic assemblies coexist with compact but reactive carbonyl, amine and fluorinated ring families
molecular.overall_character: The current three-seed panel contains 900 entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, with complete paired Parent n-fc2c108a5253 trajectories. Aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.9138 to 0.9862 and ring-closure presence from 0.9644 to 0.9908. Charge and stereocentre token presence are 0.0 throughout. These counters report SMILES features, not aromatic atom fractions, actual ionization or feasible stereochemistry. The output spans compact aza-lactams and aryl carbonyl compounds, large aromatic heterocycle assemblies, polyamines attached to constrained rings, expanded cyclic dicarbonyl systems and fluorinated imino/carbonyl polycycles. Tiny fragments coexist with extensive repeated-module growth. This is especially visible in deco_hop, with mean SMILES length 105.0 and maximum 242; high and final molecules contain many linked aromatic or nitrogen-dione units. Compared with the Parent, broad chemical themes persist while ring topology and substituents change. N-F, peroxides, cumulene imines, unusual sulfur bonding and unspecified ring junctions remain material limitations. Overall synthesis is questionable and drug-like quality weak, although some conventional carbonyl and amine subseries are much more plausible than the extreme products. Diversity across seeds is moderate, with related families dominating late output.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-1 molecule is a moderately sized aryl-substituted aza-lactam with alkyl groups and an O-linked cumulated imine side chain. Other high members are fused oxygen/nitrogen heterocycles carrying aryl thioester, ketone or amide groups. Seed 2 retains indole-carboxamide and fused lactam relatives. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9793 and halogen presence is 0.8184. The core carbonyl/heteroaromatic chemistry is recognizable, but N-O bridges, cumulene imines and unusual fused-ring arrangements complicate complete synthesis. Compared with the Parent ketone/amide and sulfur-containing ring families, the successful region still centres on bounded aromatic carbonyl structures.
liabilities: Cumulated imine, N-F and thioester functionality introduces reactivity or stability concerns despite familiar carbonyl fragments.
Constrained oxygen/nitrogen ring fusion, occasional peroxide-containing relatives and tiny fragmented products limit chemical coherence.
missing_features: Stable alternatives to the cumulated imine and N-O-containing fused linkages are underrepresented around the favorable aryl/carbonyl arrangement.
Configurations of stereogenic lactam or fused-ring centres and geometric isomers are unspecified; a unique required target fragment cannot be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best aryl aza-lactam/cumulated-imine molecule scores 0.4470018114651393 versus the Parent seed-1 maximum of 0.4126819838532174. Fluorinating its terminal imine nitrogen gives 0.41930905650182426. Other current seeds have lower maxima than their paired Parents, although fused aryl thioester and ketone members reach 0.4238198477630873 and 0.4207408531749377. Tiny fluorosulfur, hydrocarbon and fluoroalkene fragments score 0.0. The evidence favors the complete aromatic/carbonyl arrangement over fragment-sized products and does not show a general need for reactive nitrogen fluorination.

per_task.generated_character: The highest seed-1 structures are large multiaryl aza-heterocycles containing cyclic carbonyl or imino groups, ether links, fluorinated aromatic partners and a fused cyclic sulfide. Closely scoring variants add more aromatic rings, aryl peroxide connections or hypochlorite O-Cl. Seeds 0 and 2 generate repeated nitrogen-dione/aza-aromatic assemblies with carbonyl, N-N, ester or thioester links, including N-Cl/N-F variants. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9862 and halogen presence is 0.7586. The Parent also generated expanded heterocyclic assemblies; the current high region remains heavily aromatic and often much larger than conventional small-molecule frameworks. Whole-molecule synthesis is doubtful despite recognizable individual rings.
liabilities: Large repeated aromatic assemblies create severe size, solubility, flexibility and synthetic-complexity liabilities.
Peroxide, O-Cl, N-halogen, thioester and constrained unsaturation variants add chemical instability or reactivity.
missing_features: Compact accessible versions of the favorable heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangement are poorly represented among the very large late products.
Stable replacements for aryl peroxide, N-halogen and labile multicarbonyl/thioester linkages are not systematically demonstrated at comparable attachment geometry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best seed-1 assembly scores 0.6112877583465819 versus the paired Parent maximum of 0.6324703199409752; all current paired maxima are lower. Contracting its cyclic sulfide ring gives the same 0.6112877583465819. Larger peroxide/polyaryl variants score 0.6104792370120253 or 0.6100296233601354, so their added complexity is not consistently rewarded. Related ordinary versus cumulated unsaturation variants tie at 0.6087949743003997. Tiny hypochlorite, fluorinated and nitrogen fragments score 0.5. The recurring heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangement matters, but these plateau-like differences do not establish a need for repeated module growth or reactive linking groups.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest seed-0 family combines fluorinated/chlorinated aromatic rings, a branched polyamine side chain and a tightly fused nitrogen/sulfur ring system. Its exocyclic carbon-sulfur double bond is attached to a sulfur atom that also has ring bonds, rather than being an ordinary terminal thione. A carbon analogue and less fused nitrogen-ring relatives also score well. Seed 1 contains aminoalcohol/cyclobutane compounds with aryl peroxide, while seed 2 favors bulky halogenated aryl amines and cyclic aminals. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9747 and halogen presence is 0.9908. The Parent already reached high scores with aromatic amines; the current strongest family adds more unusual sulfur and constrained geometry.
liabilities: Multiply substituted sulfur with a carbon-sulfur double bond and tightly fused small rings raise stability and geometric concerns.
Aryl peroxides, heavy halogenation, excessive aromatic/amine growth and unspecified stereochemistry remain liabilities across the seeds.
missing_features: Stable conventionally bonded ring systems preserving the successful aromatic/polyamine spacing are underrepresented despite the favorable matched carbon analogue.
Defined ring-junction and side-chain configurations, together with relevant amine protonation alternatives, are absent from the displayed comparisons.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The current maximum is 0.9588472066915413 versus 0.9908331648929692 for Parent seed 0; the other current paired maxima are also lower. In a matched related pair, the carbon-based exocyclic-methylene ring scores 0.9397317511626203, above the sulfur counterpart at 0.8659731726809178. Thus unusual sulfur is not necessary for a high-scoring aromatic/polyamine arrangement. Early acidic amide chemistry scores 0.000719339566735797, and small isolated aromatic or oxygenated fragments also score poorly. A large doubled amine/aryl final product scores 0.04592415123929657, showing that adding another similar module can lose the favorable arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-2 family links a quinoline or naphthalene-like aromatic group through a short alkyl chain to an expanded nitrogen-rich cyclic dicarbonyl system. It contains several N-methyl groups, an exocyclic amino/enamine region and, in relatives, a saturated version of that region. Other seeds retain fused aromatic lactam/dione frameworks. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9782 and ring-closure presence is 0.9908. The most successful current family is comparatively recognizable and less densely fused than many other outputs, although a large heterocyclic ring still requires controlled synthesis. The Parent seed-2 chemistry already combined an aza-aromatic group with an expanded nitrogen/carbonyl ring.
liabilities: Expanded N-methyl-rich cyclic carbonyl systems may be conformationally complex and synthetically demanding.
Growth into more fused frameworks and fragment-sized proposals adds complexity or loses the intact favorable arrangement without a consistent score benefit.
missing_features: Accessible simpler cyclic dicarbonyl and linker variants preserving the aromatic/polar-group spacing are underexplored relative to repeated or tightly fused alternatives.
Configurations of saturated amino-bearing and fused-ring relatives are unspecified, and the output does not establish which conformations are relevant.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best quinoline-linked cyclic dicarbonyl scores 0.21523191119058618 versus the paired Parent seed-2 maximum of 0.21037674112349405. A shorter linker gives 0.21350507156602996, and a saturated relative gives 0.20678693060961814. The current maxima for the other seeds are below their Parents. Tiny hydrocarbon, acetylene or halogen fragments reach 0.0, while intact aromatic/polar-ring structures occupy the higher region. Linker length, saturation and nitrogen placement are tolerated to differing degrees; the modest variation does not identify a uniquely required target fragment.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-1 molecules are moderately sized fluorinated imino/carbonyl nitrogen heterocycles attached to a densely bridged, unsaturated carbon framework with an exocyclic imine. Leaders often contain N-F as well as carbon-bound fluorine; methylated and N-Cl relatives are also present. Other seeds produce acyclic urea/formamide/enamine arrangements or fused phenolic nitrogen-carbonyl systems. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9138 and halogen presence is 0.6092. Large doubled aromatic/dione assemblies occupy the very low-scoring tail. Compared with the Parent fluorinated carbonyl/nitrogen families, the strongest current seed has a more constrained imino-containing ring geometry with unresolved stereochemistry and reactive N-F.
liabilities: N-F, N-Cl and imine functionality adds reactivity or hydrolytic concerns to already constrained structures.
Densely bridged unsaturated carbon rings, unspecified configurations and repeated dione growth leave synthetic and physicochemical feasibility unresolved.
missing_features: Stable accessible counterparts preserving the favorable fluorinated imino/carbonyl arrangement without N-F and dense bridged unsaturation are not demonstrated among the leaders.
Configurations at the fluorinated bridge junctions and imine geometry are absent, while doubled late products do not preserve the compact favorable arrangement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best fluorinated bridged molecule scores 0.6214224014013073 versus the Parent seed-1 maximum of 0.5845583988949146; the other current paired maxima are lower. A close analogue missing a carbon-bound fluorine scores 0.5835441350528505. Changing ring N-F to N-methyl gives 0.5172382576037314, while N-Cl gives 0.4797103796316896. The series therefore responds strongly to local fluorination and imino/carbonyl placement, including preference for a reactive N-F motif in this comparison. Large coupled aromatic/dione products can score 1.6758614448245604e-53. These observations do not demonstrate a stable accessible pharmacophore or stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest extremes include small hydrocarbon/halogen fragments and repeated multiaryl or nitrogen-dione products. One set has mean SMILES length 105.0 and maximum 242; large coupled products elsewhere reach scores as low as 1.6758614448245604e-53.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator continues to span tiny fragments and oversized repeated assemblies rather than consistently preserving useful molecular scale.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide compact recombination, linker shortening and removal of duplicated modules while preserving useful aromatic, carbonyl and amine attachment patterns. Repeated growth should not dominate the alternatives to an intact favorable scaffold.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Leaders and close relatives contain cumulated imines, N-F/N-Cl, aryl peroxides and multiply substituted sulfur with a carbon-sulfur double bond. A matched carbon analogue scores 0.9397317511626203 versus 0.8659731726809178 for its sulfur counterpart; another series instead rewards N-F over N-methyl.
transferable_gaps.gap: Reactive or unconventional bonding remains entangled with otherwise favorable molecular arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand stable matched nitrogen, oxygen, sulfur and carbon linkages, and represent chemical compatibility independently of scalar feedback. Different local score preferences make general stable-alternative generation more useful than assuming every high-scoring reactive group is necessary.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Stereocentre-token presence is 0.0 throughout despite aryl-substituted lactams, branched polyamines, saturated amino-bearing rings and fluorinated bridged imines. Dense fusion and constrained unsaturation occur repeatedly among leaders.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces constrained and stereogenic ring systems without resolving their configurations or accessible geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support accessible ring-size and fusion alternatives plus consistent configuration assignment and stereoisomer variation. The current unspecified molecules cannot establish stereochemical score sensitivity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Cyclic-sulfide ring variants share 0.6112877583465819; ordinary versus cumulated unsaturation variants share 0.6087949743003997. A shorter-linker cyclic dicarbonyl at 0.21350507156602996 is close to its longer-linker counterpart at 0.21523191119058618.
transferable_gaps.gap: Simplification remains underexplored in favorable regions that already tolerate ring and linker changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate simpler stable ring, linker and substituent variants around established arrangements. Such variants can make score-tolerant regions more chemically interpretable and accessible without naming or requiring a particular objective.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
